page.layout: One page of text in two parts: a running head with a Latin couplet at the top above a rule; below it a French poem (heading X. GAL.) in one block, then a Latin poem (heading LAT.) in one block. No margin notes. Page number top right.

main_text.p:
Incerta, fient pertinaci
Depofita leuitate certa.
main_text.head: X. GAL.
main_text.p:
I'Ay veu, i'ay veu que le Monde eft vn fonge,
Lors que la voix de Dieu m'a resueillé:
Car il n'y a au Monde que menfonge:
L'œil y eft clos, & l'esprit trauaillé:
Tout y eft nuict : l'home y eft hors de l'home,
Se repaiffant de vaine opinion:
Et ne fentant fa propre paffion,
Ne voudroit pas qu'on luy ropist fon fomme.
main_text.head: LAT.

p.i:
Nostris quæ Superûm vox sonat auribus:
Quæ nostris tenebras pectoribus quatit:
Mortalesque simul fortior excitat
Somno lethifero obrutos.
Hæc mundum simulem dicit imagini,
Quam noctiurna solent pingere somnia.
Hæc monstrat, teneras gestiat ut leui
Mentes fallere gaudio.
Vt, dum multiplici munere vescimur
Terra, nox oculis perpetua incubet
Nostris: atque nigra nube premens vetet
Verum cernere tramitem.
Hîc noctes rigidus follicitat labor,

page.notes: The French and Latin poem lines are printed in italic and roman as shown; the Latin heading "LAT." and "X. GAL." are small-capital headings. Possible doubtful readings: "ropist" (likely "ropist" = "rompit"), "Terra," and "vetet", "simulem" (possibly "similem" in print), "Hæc monstrat" line 1 of the last stanza group ends at "leui" without a full stop. Stains and show-through from the reverse page are not transcribed. The bottom of the page is blank below the last line apart from show-through.
